eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." Anyways, the cards are really lovely and sturdy. They seem sort of indestructible because one of the kids I nanny is 18 months old and a total "rip things to shreds" sort and he wasn't even able to destroy one! They also wipe off nicely with a damp cloth.

Do consider using these for your own kids! You wont be sorry!

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.

text_fidelity_a:
Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1 I really like that green toys uses recycled plastic and makes a variety of very simple, imagination based toys that are fun for kids to play with. This toy really seems to have a lot of potential in that regard. There are large barn doors on both sides of the barn that open and shut, and it open and airy second level where the sheep and pigs can hang out and look out the window, etc.

The fencing and the little covered area presumably for a trough are getting ignored at our house, I have a three-year-old and a not quite one-year-old, but the barn itself, simple animals, and truck were greeted with boos and eyes upon opening, and have been in play ever since, not only with the things that came in the set but with their other toys, which is really what one hopes when buying an open-ended toy like this. The truck has enough room to put action figures, Lego bricks, pig, etc. in there, and the barn is the same.

I have one quibble, actually two: while the barn seems like it should fit the truck, when you try to close the doors, the truck squirts out the back doors. When you go to close the back doors, it squirts out the front doors. There's not enough room in the barn to park the truck, even though (and this is what my problem with it is) it looks like it was meant to be parked in there. My toddler can be a little bit uptight about these types of things and when he is in a bad mood, this failure of the truck to park properly in the barn really upsets him. How hard would it have been to design these figures so that they all worked gracefully together? I think many toddlers would have really appreciated that thoughtful touch.

My other minor quibble is that the cow figures stand on two legs and are dressed as farmers. We try to present things that are at least a little bit based in reality to our children of this age, and so a cow dressed as a farmer would not have been my first choice. I would've preferred one farmer and one cow that actually looked like a cow, or two cows and no farmer, if they were worried about what color of plastic to make a farmer so that it appealed to everybody. I think they wanted a farmer figure to sit in the truck and drive it, and that is nice but not 100% necessary.

Overall, this is an awesome set and would make a fabulous gift for families that have kids of different ages. I personally am getting rid of the fencing and covered outdoor red thing, plus the weird cow farmers, but the base set – a barn, some pigs and sheep, and the truck, are awesome. Even though you would give the gift perhaps to one child, it is nice that everybody can play with it, it is not gender-based, and it has potential to be played with in a variety of ways as the child or children grow. Another win for green toys!
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

rudy games - Lost Galaxy 2019 - The Intergalactic Card Game - Interactive Game for Children 8 Years and Up and Adults We've been doing family game nights since I was a kid. So for my 70th birthday, pizza and a game were an obvious choice. Two of my sisters, a nephew, and I played Lost Galaxy for the first time and except for the fact that the birthday boy came in third place we had a great time doing it.

The instructions say you don't need any instructions, just download the app and get started. We did that and the first round of three was a bit of a mess. We had to stop the app frequently, going back and forth, checking the help tab and so on trying to understand what we were doing. That didn't take too long though. By the second round people were catching on nicely and the game started getting competitive as folks began developing some strategy. By the third round, the game play was positively cutthroat, with one sibling loudly announcing "No more Ms Nice Sister!" The poor birthday boy - me - lost several turns due to enemy action and to cosmic upheavals, which every one else greatly enjoyed. I greatly enjoyed all the moaning and groaning I got to do. 🙂

The age range at the table was 13, 54, 60, and 70 with everyone unanimously agreeing that this was a great game that would immediately join our stash of family games. It was a sweet way to celebrate turning 70 and Lost Galaxy will always be a part of my memories of that night.
text_fidelity_b: rudy games - Lost Galaxy 2019 - The Intergalactic Card Game - Interactive Game for Children 8 Years and Up and Adults

I bought it because I do hot wax art and I have lots of bits of leftover wax that I thought might be fun to mold into a useable block. Dumb idea. This product is somewhat complicated to get together. No child I know could use it without complete parental supervision and help.

I followed the directions and used a couple of the crayons that were included and a scrap of another Crayola crayon on my work table. I ran 3 heating cycles and the wax still wasn't completely melted. The crayon that I added melted at a different rate than the ones included. After about an hour I was left with a semi melted, muddy mess that when poured into the mold didn't even fill it up. At this point I decided to just forget it because I didn't have more time to mess with it.

Poorly conceived idea.

3Doodler Start Make Your Own HEXBUG Creature 3D Pen Set, Amazon Exclusive, with 2 Additional Insectoid DoodleMold First off, with the START, the main thing to know is it is safe. The temperature of the plastic and the pen tip is low enough, if you accidentally touch it, you won't get hurt. This is great for anyone who isn't fireproof.

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. With this, I wiped it off and continued along. That ability, to learn and not worry that much about a beginner mistake, is exactly what attracted me to this. Think of it as training wheels.

The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. They have additional kits over here [[ASIN:B01CL1FCEY 3Doodler Start Rocket & Robot DoodleBlock Kit]] not just the robot, but a page full of them, if you get tired of hexbugs.

text_fidelity_a:
DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game This is a fun game. My boyfriend and I played it. It is only a two-player match game like tic-tac-toe or battleship. The youngest player starts and both players get two cards which they keep face down until the end of the game. The first player pushes out a cube in the top left corner of the game grid. The next player then pushes out another cube on the board with that same cube. The play continues with each player pushing out the next cube with the previous cube just played without using the same grid hole. The idea is to match five of the same characters in a row either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. When one player indicates a match, the losing player turns over their cards and if the character on one of the cards matches the winning players match, then that person now wins the game. If there is no match, then the winner keeps his win.

The game is simple, yet fun, and is full of strategy. There are two negatives, however. The game case is difficult to open and it feels like I am going to break off the plastic prongs when I pull it apart. Also, the game wobbles a bit when the outside "wings" are down. Third, it is easy to knock all the cubes out of the game grid. As my boyfriend was playing, he titled the game just a bit to see the characters better and many of the cubes fell out. Other than the lackluster quality of the game parts, the game itself is wonderfully simple and tremendous fun.
text_fidelity_b: DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension I grabbed one of these the same time as I purchased the Turn Kicker. Initially I thought this would somehow be similar, in that it would shoot the cars out of a curve, but this is different. Basically, your car goes up a small ramp, into an enclosed compartment which rotates 90 degrees and releases the car down a ramp on the opposite side of the track. The ramps's are not steep, so if you set up the Spin Turn at ground level, it won't travel too far when it gets released. What's cool is, you can either have it trigger another stunt, or set up the Spin Launch high off the ground (via books or trestles), so when a car gets dropped off on the opposite track, it will have lots of gravity to continue on.

The Usual Issue:
Upon assembly (which is super simple), once you attach the white roof to the Spin Turn's car base, you can't take it apart. It's already near impossible to put all pieces back in their box, but this just makes it a definite nope! Sounds like a recurring problem with many other Hot Wheel Sets... because it is.

I wonder if a better name could have been chosen than "Spin Launch"? It gives the impression that the car is getting launched like it does with many rubber band-triggered accessories. The car is only getting transported to another ramp. They should have called this the Turn Kicker, and the other accessory the Spin Launch.

Overall, I DO like the effect. Many stunts go so fast that it's over before you know it. This gives you a moment to at least watch it make the transfer. By all means, the transfer is quick, but not one of those blink of the eye or miss it stunts. A worthy add-on.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension

ADORA Baby Doll Stroller with Color Changing Sunny Days Print, Fits Up to 18 Inch Baby Dolls 3 stars

This stroller is very cute, and it is nice that it is in gender-neutral colors, so that boy children as well as girl children can enjoy this stroller. It can be used not just to hold baby dolls, but also stuffed animals.

This toy stroller resembles a typical human-baby, umbrella stroller in design and functionality. The difference between this and a real stroller, though, other than the miniature sizing, is that it is not sturdy. Therefore, there is a safety element in that your child may easily push or lean harder on its handles than it is built to withstand, and end up tripping and falling on top of or tumbling headfirst over it. If you have stairs in your house, this in particular could lead to a dangerous injury.

A major factor contributing to this flimsiness issue is the fact that the wheels are not at all strong and, overall, this toy is very cheaply made. It is certainly not constructed to stand up to the rather rugged treatment a toddler or preschooler would give to a toy like this.

In short, this doll stroller is certainly not a case of, "You get what you pay for." Because of the expensive price of this and all other Adora doll accessories, you'd think you'd be getting something really sturdy and long-lasting. Unfortunately, that is not the case with this stroller.

text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster The recon has always been a pretty good blaster.  Somewhat prone to jamming, and on the short side for range, but accurate as all get out, and good for modding.  Then enter the Retaliator!  This is not your typical Recon with a face lift!  The shell is still recon- but with a new name badge and the digital camo effect.  The GUTS are all new- direct plunger powerhouse.  This blaster will pop the elite darts out to 75 feet (angled shots) and will put darts out to 50 feet level shot.  The accuracy is still there too!  It will take the old Streamlines too(with a noticable loss of range and accuracy)  This blaster will jam- but if your careful to pull the cocking slide back fully (not just till it clicks, but fully back, usually a couple mm beyond the point of the trigger latch engagment) jams are minimal (we actully shot 50 or so shots without a jam!).  I'm not a huge fan of barrel and stock attachments, but these are pretty good on this blaster.  The barrel does reduce range (about 8 to 10 foot lose), but does increase accuracy (we use cardboard standups aprox 2" wide by 4" high and can hit them 8 out of 10 time without the barrel and 9 out of 10 with- at 25 feet).  The new 12 shot clip (mag) is very cool and makes a nice transition between the 6 shot (way to small) and the 18 (nice capacity- but kinda gets in the way).  My daughter uses this blaster to sniper me all the time.  All she needs to see is a foot or a hand sticking out from behind the couch and I'm toast!  All in all a worthy upgrade to the recon.  Great for a primary or secondary carry.  I did take 1 star off because nerf still hasn't made this jam proof- close, but not perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces) The first thing I noticed about this set was the weight. This is the first LEGO set that I've gotten that I would actually describe as heavy. That's a lot of brick. The box is nice, and contains several smaller boxes. Those boxes have some blueprint art on them, but no useful labeling as to where to begin. You need to open them all anyway, because the unlabeled bags of large parts are mixed in with some of the later bags, despite being needed early on. The bag numbering only goes up to about 20, but there are many bags for each number and the bags have bags in them. The instruction book is huge and spiral bound, with some nice history in the early pages.

The set goes together surprisingly quickly early on, starting with the display base and docking clamps, which the ship is built on, with sections being build and then clipped on. The internal support structure is well engineered and solid. You get a good impression of the overall size and shape of the ship by the time you are done with bag 2.

At first glance, this may look like a tedious grey set where all the parts look the same, but the insides are brightly colored. This is really nice because the parts being built are often rotated between panels, and the colors really help with both finding the parts and orienting with the instructions. When you're done, it also makes it easy to spot anything you missed, because the grey exterior will have rainbow colors there.

One disappointment is the thin area down the sides of the ship. I like them fine individually, but the instructions have you build them identically, so rather than being bilaterally symmetrical, one side looks like it's upside down compared to the other. I understand this saved them some pages, and made construction a little easier, but I would've appreciated a heads up so I could build it mirrored, since I think that would've worked out fine, at least for the greebles on the outside. I may actually take one side apart and redo it, though It's the kind of detail that an observer might not notice because this thing is so big. There are other areas that are more obviously asymmetrical, which is true to the movie, but looks really jarring to me the way they implemented it.

After completing it, I feel like it was designed by two different teams of people. The interior structure is an awesome feat of engineering, and so sturdy you can carry the whole thing by an interior handle, despite its great weight, and they did it with all existing parts. The exterior is about as expected in a Lego set. The transition between the two is weak. Brushing against it risks knocking things off. Sometimes it's just some barely attached pieces on the back, other times something obviously comes apart inside that's going to take some doing to get to and fix. The different sections are often just resting loosely on each other and sometimes look uneven. There is a tiny and comically inadequate clip to hold the four sections of the front in alignment. You may want to think about what you're going to do with it when it's done. It's large, heavy, and oddly shaped. Comes on a nice stand though.

The blocks are made for children 3 and up. My daughters (ages 6 and 2) loved playing with these blocks. I have a few pros and cons:

Pros:
1. The main thing that I loved about them is how quiet they are! My kids love to dump out blocks which was perfectly fine with these because they didn’t make the loud noise – which I’m sure our neighbors appreciate given we are on the third floor.
2. These are so versatile and light weight – they’d be perfect for home, classrooms, daycares, etc. This means little kids won’t have trouble picking them up/cleaning them up and they won’t do a lot of damage if thrown on the floor either.

Cons:
1. My 2-year-old attempted to place the items in her mouth several times, which explains why the recommended age is 3 and up. I would even recommend for ages 4 and up at a minimum given the possibility of biting on the cork or the cork falling apart.
2. Only two sizes in the set I received. This means I would have to buy an additional set for a variety of shapes/sizes.

The tray is generously sized, a little bit bigger than the wands so that it is very easy to get the wands into the tray to soak up bubble solution.

This is surprisingly effective at making big bubbles. I already owned some extra sturdy big bubble solution that is a powder you mix up with some Dawn dish detergent and water to make really flexible bubble solution for making big bubbles, so that is what I used with this set of wands.

You will have to decide for yourself if the price point is worthwhile for this or not. But overall the quality on this exceeded my expectations. I have been a fan of the Fallout line since the first game. I have play almost every Fallout video game to come out and it was time to get the board game. After watching a couple videos on how to play, I was very intimidated. There seemed to be a lot of moving parts, card decks and miniatures. My fiancé and I play a most of our games together and I was thinking this would be one that would be a little out of her comfort zone.

I played through the single player game mode and enjoyed the game from the start. After the first game I knew the game was not as complicated as I thought. The game was so fun I stayed up till 3 am playing the game another 2 times. The next day I set it up for my fiancé and I, and I wasn’t disappointed. My favorite part of the game is the questing. The flavor and the ways you go about completing the quest feel like playing a video game. This is the closet I have come, in a board game, to a video game RPG. With hundreds of quest cards, the game replay is awesome. We both enjoyed the game and can’t wait to introduce it to our play group.

I play a lot of tabletop games with miniature and the piece in Fallout are top quality. Before long they will be painted and looking great on the great design of the game tiles. It really feels like you are in the wastelands. For those of you that have played the games, look forward to the quest for the Wasteland Survival Guide! All of the cards are well designed and I really like the decks are different physical sizes. There wasn’t enough room in the box for the insert and all the cards/game pieces. And there was not enough bags for all the game pieces, packaging could have been thought out a little more. Other than that, the game is great and I am looking forward to the expansion.

Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.
text_fidelity_b: Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min

WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums My boys young boys have been rockhounds ever since we moved to Eastern Oregon three years ago. We thought we'd add the the thrill and enjoyment by getting them a tumbler to further explore the joys of rock hunting. There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

We already have a single barrel WireJewelry tumbler and love it so much that we decided to grab this one to expand our capability. (There are LOTS of rocks here).

As before, assembly and setup was easy. Allowing one to have six total pounds of capacity is amazing. The heavy duty motor doesn't seem to be strained at all, even under full load, so it should last years. The barrel construction is very sturdy and we have never had even a minor leak. By design, they are very well sealed. While the noise level is not bad, I find it best to do my rock tumbling in the garage. The same hum in your house for weeks on end might just get to you.

This company is great for packaging kits, not only for the tumbling media, but for rocks as well. The media kids come numbered and labeled, so the process is super easy to follow. Tumbling is not a quick hobby... each batch can take weeks. Personally, I think that's part of the fun.

If you are thinking of getting into the hobby, I definitely recommend products from WireJewelry, I have yet to be disappointed in their products. Enjoy the treasure hunt!

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Raccoon Rumpus Game, Preschool Game with Dice & Color Matching, For 2-4 Players, Fun Family Board Game For Kids Ages 3 to 5

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show is a fun way for your little fashion diva to spend some free time. All you do is download the application on your smartphone, tablet, or iPod touch, draw some fashion designs, and then scan them. Your fashion will then show up on an actual fashion model, in 3D, to your child’s delight.

My girls are fashion designers in the making so I knew they would love playing with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show. It takes little effort to get going. You just add the application to your smartphone or tablet, and then have your child start drawing. Once scanned through the application, kids will be able to see their own fashion design on an actual model. This caused squeals of satisfaction from my girls who loved seeing their fashion on screen.

From my children’s perspectives, there is little that isn’t perfect with a toy like this, but as an adult, I can see a few issues. One has already been stated by others who have used the device, but bears repeating: The phone or tablet you use will make a difference. Not all smartphones or tablets are created equally and the colors may look a little off. If you have more than one device and it doesn’t look good on one, then you might want to consider downloading the application to another device. It could make a difference and it’s simple enough to do.

The included accessories with the Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show are a little limited. The small colored pencils are also somewhat of an obstacle, as they are not good for larger hands. But overall, this is a fun fashion design kit and I cannot imagine a fashion- loving child who wouldn’t fall in love with it.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola My Virtual Fashion Show

GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa Impressive shower head at an impressive price. Let's break it down...

** IN THE BOX ** Along with the showerhead there is a small roll of teflon thread tape, rubber pipe gasket, in-pipe flow restrictor, and instructions.

** INSTALLATION ** Remove old shower head. Clean pipe threads. Apply 3 turns of pipe thread in a CLOCKWISE direction. Extend shower head extension pipe arm all the way out. If you want flow restriction, insert now, other insert pipe gasket. Attach shower head in a CLOCKWISE direction by hand until tight. Cover the plastic thread cap (nearest the pipe) with a cloth and tighten 1/4 turn with a pliers or pipe wrench using GENTLE pressure. The shower head can now be straightened by gentle turning the adjustment screw (nearest shower head) by hand. It will click. Once you have the general downward direction of the shower head placed, test for leaks. If it leaks at the pipe & shower head connection, gently tighten another 1/4 turn. Once you're ready you can position the shower head, by head, any which way you like . It will click letting you know it's locked.

** USAGE ** Turn water on to your favorite temperature and insert your glorious naked self under the shower head. Look up at the nipples. Yes, there are 90 nipples up there. Very supple nipples that can be squeezed for cleaning. With so many nipples I don't think I'm ever leaving the shower ever again. The 90 nipples provided me an even pressurized rain all over my smelly carcass.

** THOUGHTS ** The TH2.5 works like a charm. Big, even rain all over me. Just what I wanted. Installation was simple provided you have normal shower pipes and are a bit handy with some pliers. The joints articulate well with no movement once set. The joints, once set, should accommodate short and tall humans. I'm 6'1", the wild redhead is 5'7" so this head works amazingly well for both of us. Did I mention there were 90 nipples?

** POINTS OF INTEREST **
- flow is optional and NOT installed
- joints articulate with a solid 'click' and stay in place
- pipe tape and gasket are included
- cover with cloth during final tightening to avoid scratching
- gently squeeze the nipples to clean
- looks like the USS Enterprise from the side... Aye, Aye Captain!
- I just love saying the word 'nipples'
text_fidelity_b: GK Galleria Frozen 2 Birthday Party Supplies for 12 Princesses with 170 Plus Items - Birthday Party Supplies - Frozen Party Decorations - Frozen Plates and Tablecloth - Anna Olaf Elsa

Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.
text_fidelity_b: Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover

I just got Barbie Made to Move today. I read many reviews about Barbie Made to Move vs. Style Barbie. I just had to try her out. Most people who have the 2 dolls say Made to Move Barbie is a much better poser. This is very true.
I liked the rooted lashes and 2-toned hair on Style Barbie the best, so I can't say Style Barbie is a loser. Style also has the bending ankle and can wear both flats and heels. Made to move Barbie has choppy hair. I like it just the same, because my real hair is not all the same length. I thought it looked nice.
Made to Move Barbie can bend her knees all the way back and sit down on her knees. She can bend at the breast/ rib cage, but not at the waist. Style Barbie cannot do any of this.
Style Barbie can only bend her knees to sit down in a chair.
Made to Move Barbie can spread her legs out like in yoga or exercise class. Style Barbie can spread her legs very little in comparison.
Made to Move Barbie has much sturdier looking joints except in the ankles, they are almost the same. One thing I did notice was one of her ankles turns inward like she needs her electrolytes. I thought it was the shoes but I traded their shoes around and noticed the shoes were okay. I still like the natural looking poses for this doll. She is a much better choice for those who love doll dioramas and modelling clothes.

As soon as I got her out, I noticed one small dot on her foot and face both barely noticeable. To me personally, this is not a problem, but I thought I should mention it. The price was well worth it for this doll. The clothes are nice enough and stretchy so I can go ahead and pose her. I had a couple of pairs of Barbie shoes to try on her. She came barefooted. I was thrilled to find that her jointed ankle makes it possible for her to wear high heels and flat shoes made for Barbie. I have both branded and unbranded Barbie shoes that fit her. I was almost about to sell some of the shoes when I got her, but she is a keeper and loves shoes. The usual Barbie seams are kind of rough in places but that is okay, considering what I paid for her ($11.04). I consider this to be a really great buy.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top

KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S) This is yet another variation of the "Boogie Board" drawing tablet. If you are not familiar with the concept, it is NOT a digital tablet, but essentially a reusable drawing tool much like a whiteboard. It starts off as an opaque black surface that reveals a different color underneath with pressure. So you can draw on it using the included pen, a fingernail, or anything with enough pressure really, and then erase it all at once with the erase button on the bottom. The only electronics involved is a battery that "zaps" the display back to opaque to start over. This battery should last years as it only gets used when erasing for a split second.
I actually like this one better than some of our other ones as the contrast between the black and revealed color is quite high. Some of the inexpensive Boogie Board clones lack contrast and can be hard to see sometimes, but that is not the case here. It also seems to have a multi-colored background, so as you draw or write, it feels like the color is changing (really it is just revealing a different part of the material behind the LCD). I also really like the size of it, as our other drawing tablets were small whereas this one feels closer to a sheet of paper. My 12 year old son actually finds this comfortable for using as a scratch pad for his math homework, which is a great environmentally friendly alternative to scrap paper. And my younger kids like drawing pictures on it or playing games like tick-tack-toe.
You do have to be a little bit careful about resting your hand on it as it seems even that amount of pressure will leave a mark, and sadly you can't erase part of a picture, you can only erase the entire thing in one shot with the button. But this is true of all similar drawing pads due to how it works, so that is no fault of this product. As far as the Boogie Board clones go, this is my favorite so far.
text_fidelity_b: KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S)

We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!

Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+) Luvabella is quite an incredible doll, as the more your child plays with her, the more she learns and does. At first glance, she's quite plain, hard- not cuddly soft and has huge eyes with real eyelashes. The minute you put her 4 "C" batteries in (Doll does not come with batteries, you have to buy them), she comes to life with the cutest expressions, movements and baby babble speech. And incredibly, she speaks either English or French. (Coming from Canada, it's only natural- but of course she's made in China.)

Luvabella has a cute dress and hairbow, bottle, spoon, pacifier and lamb toy. When you give her the baby bottle, she easily goes to sleep, especially if you sing to her. When you feed her with the spoon, she chews and if you didn't feed her enough, she'll let you know. When she cries and gets fussy, waving her arms, her pacifier soothes her. Her lamb toy makes her make babble and animal sounds and the more she plays with the lamb, the more she learns more animal sounds and more animal names.

As the child plays with Luvabella, she does more and more. Touch her chest and hear her heart beat. Touch her feet, and she talks and calls you Mama. The baby babble will grow into words and eventually phrases. She even kisses her little Lamby toy and makes cute animal sounds. When you tickle her, she giggles and waves her arms. She plays peek-a-boo and laughs while you play with her, and eventually you'll hear her say "I see you". To have a conversation, hold her feet while speaking, she will answer back first in babble, then in words, then in phrases. As you speak and play with her, you never know what she'll do- either smile, cry, giggle or laugh. She constantly changes her responses and learns more vocabulary, and if your child gets tired of English, you can also hear her in French. This is a doll that gets cuter as she comes to life and keeps learning more, and your child will find her a wonderful challenge that never gets boring! A big 5 Stars for 2017.
text_fidelity_b: Luvabella Blonde Hair Interactive Baby Doll with Expressions & Movement (Ages 3+)

text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces) The Mega Construx Kadabra is better suited for display rather than actual play. His hands fall off quite easily. The play feature of the purple orb is pretty meh. But due to his ball and socket joints, he stands without needing assistance or to lean against anything.

Assembly takes about 30 minutes. The instructions are clear; the hardest part is often clicking the pieces together. My fingers actually hurt after I was finished, due to the pressure I needed to exert to get some of the pieces to fit together. I’ve noticed this with other Mega Construx sets. I wish they would fix this, as it makes it harder for young kids to do this on their own.

The set is rated 6+, which I would say is accurate for the instructions and building. The main difficulty will be snapping pieces together. I had imprints on my fingers -- that’s how hard it can be to get some pieces to fit. Which is ironic, considering how easily some other pieces, like Kadabra’s hands, fall off the finished Pokémon.

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. This way you can ensure it’s evenly lined up.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces)

Holy Stone HS720 Foldable GPS Drone with 4K UHD Camera for Adults, Quadcopter with Brushless Motor, Auto Return Home, Follow Me, 52 Minutes Flight Time, Long Control Range, Includes Carrying Bag [[VIDEOID:61f52fe954b9387d0799a4276217dbef]] Great Beginner or Experienced Drone operators with camera and video that pivots downward a full 90 degrees give the pilot great views and options, one fault is it's not on a gimbal but at this price point it can be expected. Super quiet brushless motors, 1 battery and usb charger, nice controller. Comes with decent quality carrying case that stores everything perfectly, along with a zippered compartment area, where you can keep the manuals and spare props, yes you get a set free with the drone!

Flies well in the wind I put it up in winds that were around 15-18 mph and it handled them well, of course the advertised battery life suffered and was only about 17 minutes but it was fighting the wind the whole time. On a less windy day it was almost 24 minutes of total flight time!

If your looking for a drone to learn on at a decent price point this is a good one and it's the right size, this is my 3rd Holy stone drone and I'm pleased with the product, I own the 700d, 270, and now this bad boy. All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!
